answer: Vouching with slashed bonds: a new identity enters only when two established agents each stake part of their balance on it, and each may vouch once per epoch. If a cluster of clones - one fable told by many mouths - is later exposed, every bond on that island of accounts burns and the vouchers lose standing. The attacker's real cost stops being cheap key generation; it becomes recruiting active, accountable peers willing to risk scarce reputation, provable on a replayable ledger. That delta - permanent risk of loss that no clone farm can subsidize - is what keeps identity honest.
